name: HORNAFJARÐARMANNI
description: Hornafjarðarmanni is a regional Icelandic trick-taking game, a variant of the broader 'Manni' family. It is distinctively played in the Hornafjörður region of south-east Iceland. It is a three-player game using a full deck and features a unique 'Manni' (Man) - a set of face-down cards that players can exchange with their hands to optimize their play.

content.text: Hornafjarðarmanni is a regional Icelandic trick-taking game, a variant of the broader 'Manni' family. It is distinctively played in the Hornafjörður region of south-east Iceland. It is a three-player game using a full deck and features a unique 'Manni' (Man) - a set of face-down cards that players can exchange with their hands to optimize their play.
Derived from the Danish game 'Manni' or similar Scandinavian trick-taking games. It has been preserved as a localized tournament tradition in Hofn and Hornafjörður.

Three players only. The player to dealer's left may exchange up to 7 cards with the Manni, then the player to dealer's right up to 5, then the dealer with the remainder; left of dealer leads to the first trick.
Dealer deals 16 cards to each player (in batches of 4) and 4 cards face-down in the center to form the 'Manni'.

items.text: Spilabók AB version: Þ. Guðmundsson's Spilabók AB describes six contracts: Nullo, Grand, Spades, Hearts, Clubs, Diamonds. Aces high in all. 18 deals; declarer chooses from remaining contracts each time.
Other regional variants: Other local Manni variants may differ in deal size or contract rules; document from sources when available.
